parsed_output.analysis: The specification requires Power On to enter HumanDriving, Front Distance > 10 to move HumanDriving -> Autonomous, human steering cmd / brake pressed to return to HumanDriving from autonomous, and Power Off to go to a final state. The autonomous mode is a submachine with sub-states. The model misplaces the Power On trigger, creates an incorrect Power On transition out of HumanDriving, introduces an un-specified AutonomousIdle entry guarded by Front Distance <= 10, moves only from AutonomousActive back to HumanDriving instead of from the autonomous final context, and routes Power Off from HumanDriving to a disconnected AutonomousFinal state that is not part of the autonomous submachine and is not a system final state.

issues.issue: Power On transition is on the wrong edge and the start transition is unlabeled
issues.reason: Spec 3 says when power on the system turns into human driving mode. The model has an unlabeled [*] --> HumanDriving and a Power On transition from HumanDriving to Autonomous, which is the opposite direction and does not model Power On as the entry trigger to HumanDriving.
issues.where: [*] --> HumanDriving and HumanDriving --> Autonomous : Power On

issues.issue: Power Off transition source and target do not match spec
issues.reason: Spec 5 says when power off it will transit to final state. The model only allows Power Off from HumanDriving to AutonomousFinal, and AutonomousFinal is a named auto final state not a system final/terminal state, and Power Off from Autonomous is missing.
issues.where: HumanDriving --> AutonomousFinal : Power Off and state AutonomousFinal

issues.issue: Transition back to HumanDriving on human steering cmd / brake pressed is limited to AutonomousActive and does not reflect 'in (auto final)'
issues.reason: Spec 4 says transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final). The model triggers the return only from AutonomousActive, not from an autonomous final context, and AutonomousFinal has no outgoing transitions back to HumanDriving.
issues.where: AutonomousActive --> HumanDriving : Human Steering Cmd and AutonomousActive --> HumanDriving : Brake Pressed

issues.issue: Un-specified entry into autonomous sub-states with Front Distance <= 10
issues.reason: Spec does not define an AutonomousIdle state nor a Front Distance <= 10 entry condition for Autonomous. The model creates a parent-to-child transition from the submachine state Autonomous to AutonomousIdle with a guard not mentioned in the spec.

issues.issue: AutonomousFinal is disconnected from the autonomous submachine
issues.reason: Spec 2 says autonomous mode has sub-states and is represented by a sub machine state. AutonomousFinal is defined as a separate top-level state, never entered from Autonomous/AutonomousIdle/AutonomousActive, and is not a sub-state of Autonomous, so the autonomous submachine is incomplete and the final state is orphaned.
issues.where: AutonomousFinal : Auto Final State and HumanDriving --> AutonomousFinal : Power Off

issues.issue: Initial entry to Autonomous sub-states is not modeled as a submachine entry
issues.reason: Spec 4 says when front_distance > 10 auto transport to autonomous state. The model splits this into an extra idle/active split with a Front Distance > 10 transition inside the submachine, which is not specified and obscures the required direct HumanDriving -> Autonomous transition on Front Distance > 10.
issues.where: Autonomous --> AutonomousIdle : Front Distance <= 10 and AutonomousIdle --> AutonomousActive : Front Distance > 10

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
user_prompt:
## Natural-language specification

1 The human driving mode is represented by a simple state. 2 The autonomous mode has sub-states and is represented by a sub machine state. 3. when power on, the system turn into human driving mode 4when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state 4. transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final) 5 when power off, it will transit to final state

## State machine model (PlantUML)

@startuml
[*] --> HumanDriving
HumanDriving : Human Driving Mode

HumanDriving --> Autonomous : Power On
Autonomous : Autonomous Mode
Autonomous : <<submachine>>

Autonomous --> AutonomousIdle : Front Distance <= 10
AutonomousIdle : Autonomous Idle Mode

AutonomousIdle --> AutonomousActive : Front Distance > 10
AutonomousActive : Autonomous Active Mode

AutonomousActive --> HumanDriving : Human Steering Cmd
AutonomousActive --> HumanDriving : Brake Pressed

HumanDriving --> Autonomous : Front Distance > 10
HumanDriving --> AutonomousFinal : Power Off

AutonomousFinal : Auto Final State
@enduml
